transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Stratus Head of ML), Daniel Ruiz (Stratus VP Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Data Platform)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): QBR - usage up 23% QoQ, cost spike in early March due to concurrent batch for analytics job, reliability incidents 2/28 and 3/03 (short falls), roadmap priorities: SSO, private VPC for PHI workflows, perf benchmark request.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is our qbr for stratus health, we'll keep it tight 45 minutes. quick agenda, usage, cost, incidents, roadmap and next steps. olivia, you wanna kick off with any updates?
[00:15] Olivia Park: yeah thanks maya, um overall things are good, usage has increased as we rolled out the patient-summary feature, about a 20-25 percent increase month over month, but we did see a cost spike early march, not sure why exactly, daniel was looking into that.
[00:32] Daniel Ruiz: ya so to clarify we had a one-off analytics job where we hit high concurrency, it was basically reprocessing legacy transcripts and the batching was suboptimal, tokens per request were large, caused a spike in tokens and some requests timed out. we flagged it as a reliability incident 2/28.
[00:50] Ravi Patel: ok that makes sense, high concurrency plus long seq length can really push cost if prefix kv cache not leveraged. did you run that job against the hosted api or dedicated pool?
[01:03] Daniel Ruiz: hosted api. we haven't moved the heavy reprocessing to dedicated yet.
[01:08] Maya Chen: got it. one thing we can do is suggest a config for that batch job to leverage progressive batching and kv prefixing — reduces token re-compute. also we can model the cost difference if you run big jobs on Dedicated vs hosted with burst.
[01:24] Sofia Alvarez: quick q, what does dedicated look like for our SLA needs? we handle PHI and need audit logs + kms.
[01:32] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives reserved capacity and isolation, and you can run in our private deployment with customer-managed VPC and KMS. audit logs and HSM options available with the enterprise package. we'll share the SOC2 docs too.
[01:45] Olivia Park: when you say private deployment, are we talking on-prem or vpc in cloud? what about latency to our services?
[01:53] Ravi Patel: both options — private VPC (cloud-hosted in your AWS account) or on-prem appliance for air-gapped. latency depends on region and network peering; for PHI we usually recommend private VPC in same region as your apps. we can run a latency baseline as part of the benchmark.
[02:10] Daniel Ruiz: for now we want to evaluate economics: the hosted API is simpler but our monthly committed spend could justify Dedicated. can you show numbers comparing per-token hosted vs reserved Dedicated?
[02:20] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll send a per-route token cost export and a model of expected savings at different commit levels. preliminary calc shows if you commit for reserved capacity covering 60% of peak you could see ~30% net reduction in unit cost for our typical workloads, but depends on seq length and batching.
[02:36] Olivia Park: last QBR we asked about quantized models; how mature is that path? any quality regressions we should expect?
[02:44] Ravi Patel: quantization is good for cost — we have profiles for 4-bit and 8-bit on many open models, and Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization per workload. quality impact is usually minimal for retrieval-augmented prompts, but for sensitive clinical outputs we recommend running your prompt set through our eval harness. send us your top 100 prompts and we'll run regressions.
[03:02] Maya Chen: add that to action items — olivia to send prompts.
[03:06] Olivia Park: yep will do.
[03:09] [03:09] Sofia Alvarez: on the topic of security, can we confirm SSO SAML mapping for roles? we need SCIM and role-based provisioning.
[03:17] Maya Chen: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning and RBAC. we'll share the integration guide and a short checklist.
[03:25] Daniel Ruiz: also curious about monitoring — token-level cost by route, latency percentiles, per-model dashboards. is that in the console?
[03:33] Ravi Patel: yep Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdown, traces and error logs. you can set alerts for token spikes and quality regressions. we can also give you access to higher retention for logs as an add-on.
[03:45] Olivia Park: great. on incidents, you mentioned 3/03 as well? what happened there?
[03:51] Ravi Patel: that was a short backend GC spike on our side in the east region; some requests went to fallback model which slightly increased latency for a subset of your calls. SLA breach was <1 min total impact but we wanted to call it out. we've mitigated the root cause and added extra autoscaling buffer for such GC windows.
[04:12] Daniel Ruiz: ok glad that's fixed. any recommendations for us to avoid these events from client side?
[04:17] Ravi Patel: for critical flows you can pin to specific model and route or set a low-latency SLA with Dedicated and reserve capacity. also implement client-side retries with exponential backoff and use idempotency keys.
[04:29] Olivia Park: curious about the perf benchmark — what are typical parameters you test?
[04:33] Ravi Patel: we usually test across seq lengths (128, 512, 2048), batch sizes (1, 8, 32), and concurrency profiles. for GPU types we test on H100 and A100 variants and compare to quantized CPU where applicable. we'll tailor to your top prompt set and measure median P50, P95 latencies and throughput.
[04:53] Maya Chen: ok back to costs — we saw an 18% increase in tokens for the patient-summary route but cost rose 28% because of more long-context jobs. we'll include per-route CSV where you can see tokens vs cost.
[05:07] Olivia Park: when can we expect the cost export?
[05:10] Maya Chen: i'll send it by 3/24.
[05:13] Daniel Ruiz: can we also get guidance on caching? we have many similar prefixes in the patient-summary flow.
[05:19] Ravi Patel: prefix caching will help a lot; we can suggest cache TTLs and how to structure prompts for higher cache hit rates. also consider using embeddings to pre-classify and only call the LLM for unique cases.
[05:34] Sofia Alvarez: roadmap alignment — we plan to go live with a new clinician note summarization in q2; from your side any new features that would help latency or reduce cost?
[05:42] Maya Chen: on our roadmap we have improved continuous batching heuristics and a new model variant optimized for long-context clinical prompts launching in q3. Redwood Optimize will push model recommendations and quantization tips as they become stable.
[05:56] Olivia Park: that sounds promising, timeline for that long-context model? q3 you said?
[06:01] Ravi Patel: yes early q3. depends on wider validation, but we'll prioritize you for early access if you sign up for the dedicated pilot.
[06:12] Daniel Ruiz: about the pilot — what's the commit level and duration typically?
[06:17] Maya Chen: pilots are flexible but we recommend a 1-3 month reserved capacity pilot; typically a small commit to cover baseline throughput with options to scale. we can draft numbers after we run the perf benchmark.
[06:28] Olivia Park: ok can we close with recap and next steps?
[06:31] Maya Chen: sure. recap: we will send token-level cost export by 3/24; raji — ravi will propose benchmark plan by 3/26; olivia to send top prompts and failure cases by 3/25; we'll share SOC2, KMS, and SSO docs. follow ups: schedule benchmark for next week or the week after depending on your availability.
[06:49] Daniel Ruiz: thanks all. one more ask — can you include an estimated effort for SSO/SCIM integration for our infra team?
[06:56] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include an estimated effort (hours) in the SSO guide we send.
[07:02] Olivia Park: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:06] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up in email, meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
